pl-l3d32c1-d1e115.summary: Adds a treatment of God's love by which he loves us, which is not other than that by which we love him.
claims: God's love for us is the same as that by which we love him.

pl-l3d32c1-d1e118.summary: States that God's love is the divine essence; by the same love the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit love one another and us. Though his love is immutable and eternal, he loves some more and some less.
claims: God's love is the divine essence.
God loves some more and some less, though his love is immutable.

pl-l3d32c1-d1e121.summary: Quotes Augustine: God's love is incomprehensible and immutable; he loves in each of us what he made and hates what we made, and so, in a wondrous way, loves us even when he hates us. Who can say how much he loves the members of his Only-begotten, and how much more the Only-begotten himself? Scripture says he hates nothing he made.
claims: God loves what he made in us and hates what we made.
God loves the members of Christ and Christ still more.

pl-l3d32c1-d1e134.summary: Draws out that God loves all his creatures, since he hates nothing he made and all he made is very good; if he loves every good, he loves all he made. Among them he loves rational creatures more, among these the members of his Son more, and his Son much more.
claims: God loves all creatures because all are good.
God's love has degrees: creatures, rational creatures, Christ's members, Christ.

pl-l3d32c1.summary: Turns to God's love for us, which is the same as that by which we love him. God's love is the divine essence; by it the Father, Son, and Spirit love themselves and us; though immutable and eternal, he loves some more and some less. Augustine: God's love is incomprehensible and immutable, loving in each of us what he made and hating what we made, loving even when he hates, loving the members of his Only-begotten and much more the Only-begotten. So God loves all his creatures, since all he made is good, and among them more the rational ones, more still the members of his Son, and most the Son himself.
claims: God's love is the divine essence.
God loves all that he made.
God loves rational creatures more, the members of Christ more, and Christ most.
God hates what we made, sin, while loving what he made.
